title: The Crypt of Nine Hundred Steps
story: Pallastor the Gloom Custodian has swallowed all the light in the Steppe Crypt, and the pilgrims trapped inside cannot find the stairs. Mr 6 knows each lantern he lights pushes back the darkness for exactly 14 steps of corridor, and the crypt corridor runs 900 steps from door to door.
question: How many lanterns must Mr 6 light to cover all 900 steps of corridor?
hint: Divide 900 by 14 — but if there's any leftover corridor, that scrap of darkness still needs a whole lantern.
victory: The sixty-fifth lantern flared over the last four dark steps, and Pallastor shrank to a grumpy shadow the size of a mouse and scurried off to sulk behind a coffin.
imagePrompt: A towering hooded shadow custodian retreating down a vast stone crypt corridor as a chain of warm lanterns lights up behind a small numeral-six knight.
solution: Each lantern covers 14 steps, so divide: 900 ÷ 14 = 64 with a remainder of 4.
64 lanterns cover 64 × 14 = 896 steps, leaving 4 dark steps.
Those last 4 steps still need a whole lantern, so Mr 6 lights 65 lanterns.
praise: Dividing was the right instinct — the leftover 4 steps just needed one more whole lantern.
